items.title: 6.12.1 Calculating delta G for a reaction

source_refs.note: Topic 6.12.1, printed pages 139-140; Sample Problems 6.12 and 6.13 (the print numbers skip 6.10 and 6.11). The chapter exercise (pages 140-143) is not reproduced.

blocks.text: For CaSO4(s) giving Ca2+(aq) + SO4 2-(aq) at 25 degrees C, with heats of formation CaSO4(s) -1432.7, Ca2+(aq) -543.0 and SO4 2-(aq) -907.5 kJ, and standard entropies 106.7, -55.2 and +17.2 J per K: delta H = (-543.0 - 907.5) - (-1432.7) = -17.8 kJ; delta S = (-55.2 + 17.2) - 106.7 = -144.7 J per K = -0.1447 kJ per K; delta G = delta H - T delta S = -17.8 - 298 x (-0.1447) = +25.3 kJ. The process is non-spontaneous at standard conditions at 25 degrees C.

For N2(g) + 3H2(g) giving 2NH3(g) at 25 degrees C, with heats of formation N2 0, H2 0 and NH3 -45.9 kJ, and standard entropies 191.5, 130.6 and 193 J per K: delta H = 2 x (-45.9) - 0 = -91.8 kJ; delta S = 2 x 193 - (191.5 + 3 x 130.6) = -197 J per K = -0.197 kJ per K; delta G = -91.8 - 298 x (-0.197) = -33.1 kJ. Since delta G is negative, the Haber process is spontaneous at standard conditions, 25 degrees C.
